learning_objective: 🎯 Trace the incredible journey of human life from conception to old age and understand the physical, cognitive, and social changes we undergo!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Development is lifelong (from womb to tomb), multi-directional (some things grow, some decline), and highly influenced by historical and cultural contexts.
Development is a joint product of genetic inheritance (nature) and environmental influences (nurture). They interact continuously to shape who we are.
Characterized by rapid physical growth, motor development, and the formation of 'attachment' (the strong emotional bond with caregivers). Jean Piaget noted children think differently than adults.
A period of transition from childhood to adulthood. Marked by puberty, the search for identity, peer influence, and abstract thinking.
Adulthood involves establishing careers and intimate relationships. Old age involves coping with physical decline but often brings wisdom and a life review.

fun_activity.title: ⏳ My Timeline
fun_activity.instructions: Draw a timeline of your life from birth to now. Mark 3 major physical milestones (e.g., learning to walk) and 3 major social/cognitive milestones (e.g., first best friend, learning to read). Notice how development spans different domains!

exam_tips: 📌 'Development' includes both qualitative (intelligence, morality) and quantitative (height, weight) changes, whereas 'Growth' is only quantitative.
📌 Be prepared to discuss the challenges of adolescence (identity crisis, peer pressure, physical changes).
📌 Mention Jean Piaget when writing about cognitive development in childhood.
quick_recap: ⭐ Genotype is the actual genetic material, while Phenotype is the observable characteristics.
⭐ Motor development follows two principles: Cephalocaudal (head to toe) and Proximodistal (center to extremities).
⭐ The prenatal period (before birth) is highly vulnerable to teratogens (harmful environmental agents).
